# Codex CLI

OpenAI's terminal coding agent, and the second executor in [[agent-orchestrator]]. Driven as
`codex exec --json` with `-C <workspace>`, so the answer comes from a structured stream rather than
from parsed prose — the same contract as [[claude-code-cli]], reached through different flags.

## Where it differs, and why that matters

- **Sandboxing is configuration, not a mode flag**: `-c sandbox_mode=read-only |
  workspace-write | danger-full-access`, passed identically on a fresh invocation and a resumed one.
  A resume that quietly dropped the sandbox setting would be the worst kind of bug — invisible and
  privileged.
- **Text only.** It cannot open an image or extract a PDF, so [[read-capability-routing]] moves any
  subtask that declares those reads to Claude, whatever the planner asked for.
- **No plugin mechanism.** Skills reach it as files it is allowed to open plus a prompt section
  naming the index, rather than as a loaded plugin. The prompt is therefore built per *attempt*, not
  once — a prompt written for the planner's chosen agent describes the wrong mechanism after a
  fallback ([[agent-skills-checked-into-the-repo]]).

## Effort

Codex exposes a reasoning ladder with a per-model ceiling. The orchestrator clamps a request above
that ceiling instead of sending it and hoping — [[reasoning-effort-as-a-portable-label]].

## Observed failure mode

A spent subscription is the routine one, and it arrives as prose on stderr:

> "You've hit your usage limit. Upgrade to Pro (https://chatgpt.com/explore/pro), visit
> https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage to purchase more credits or try again at Aug 8th, 2026
> 9:36 AM."
> — vs-llm-orchestrator/agent-orchestrator/extension/harness/fixtures/multi-fallback.jsonl, 2026-08-07

The orchestrator quotes that verbatim rather than paraphrasing it, because the reset time is the only
part a reader can act on, and remembers the agent as exhausted for the rest of the run instead of
paying for the same refusal again.
